page.layout: Running head across top: EMBLEMATA. with page number 125 at top right. Full-width heading in two lines with roman numeral XXVI at right. Below, a woodcut emblem plate (full width, no text inside it). Below the plate, one block of verse text in full width, italic in parts.

l.i: HI colubris collubri, cristas tollente Ceraste,
Dextra secat, gladium cæli qua librat ab arce,
Quos signent rogitas? Satis & re & nomina
Quos Satan ( armauit iusti quem Numinis ira
Terrarum exitio ) funesto excivit ab Orco.
Ast hominum tandem forte miseratus acerbâ,
Exerto Verbi Christus nunc dissecat ense.

page.notes: The plate shows a circle of intertwined serpents with a sword descending from the clouds at upper right; the scene is not transcribed. Initial "H" of the verse is a large woodcut-style initial, read as H with the following I. The first verse line reads "HI colubris collubri" as printed; "Ceraste" and "Conferti" are as printed. The word "exitio" and "Orco" are read from the scan with some doubt. The final word "enfe" is printed with a long-tail mark, read as "ense" with a [?] suggested.
